questionText: What must you settle before entering data into an AI tool?

answerOptions.text: Data class, approval for tool and purpose, and whether the purpose needs every detail
Only whether the tool is paid for
Only whether training use is switched off
Only whether colleagues use the tool too

explanation: An input is acceptable only if data class, approval for exactly this combination and data minimisation all fit.

questionText: In the example model, which level does a sick note with a diagnosis belong to?

answerOptions.text: Internal
Specially protected
Public
Confidential, but allowed in any assistant

explanation: Health data is a special category under GDPR Art. 9. General assistants are blocked for it.

questionText: A colleague wants to enter a password into an approved company assistant to explain a login error. What applies?

answerOptions.text: In an approved tool that is allowed.
It is allowed if he changes the password afterwards.
Credentials never go into a prompt, at any level.
It is allowed if the history is deleted.

explanation: Passwords and API keys open systems. They are never entered; if a leak is suspected, change and report them.

questionText: You replace customer names with codes and keep the mapping list. Which is true?

answerOptions.text: The data is anonymous; data protection no longer applies.
The data is public.
The data may go into any tool.
The data is pseudonymised and stays personal data.

explanation: With additional information the person can be identified again. Such data stays personal data (GDPR Art. 4(5), Recital 26).

questionText: You have redacted a complaint. Which detail may stay in for the reply draft?

answerOptions.text: The facts of the case: twelve pumps, eight working days late
The customer's IBAN
The private mobile number
The customer's e-mail address

explanation: The draft needs the facts, not contact or payment details. What the purpose does not need stays out.

questionText: Which four building blocks make a brief checkable?

answerOptions.text: Greeting, request, thanks, sign-off
Context, task, format, limits
Length, language, font, colour
Model name, version, price, vendor

explanation: Context, task, format and limits make the result checkable. They do not make it automatically right.

questionText: An AI draft to a customer states a delivery cause that appeared nowhere. What happened?

answerOptions.text: The model looked up the cause in internal systems.
The cause was hidden in the customer e-mail.
The model filled a gap with plausible text.
That is impossible; models invent nothing.

explanation: Without limits, models fill gaps with likely-sounding details. That is why "mark what is missing" belongs in the brief.

questionText: How do you measure whether AI saves you time on reply e-mails?

answerOptions.text: On the time saving the vendor promises
On the feeling after the first try
On the length of the drafts
On your own comparison cases: handling time and corrections needed

explanation: Only your own measurements show whether draft plus review is faster than without AI.

questionText: An AI summary names an owner who does not appear in the notes. How do you treat the item?

answerOptions.text: Delete the person and mark the item as open
Keep it, the person fits the topic
Add the person to the notes afterwards
Delete the whole item, including the need

explanation: What is not in the notes is invented. The need stays as an open item until someone takes ownership.

questionText: You want to transcribe meetings automatically. You have a works council. What applies?

answerOptions.text: The licence is enough if the feature is included.
Settle purpose, information, legal basis and works council co-determination first
Only external guests need to be informed.
Co-determination applies only to video recordings.

explanation: Transcription processes personal data and can make behaviour or performance visible; in Germany the works council has a say on such systems (BetrVG § 87(1) no. 6).

questionText: What is an AI hallucination?

answerOptions.text: A program crash
A deliberate falsehood by the vendor
A convincingly worded but false or unsupported statement
A typo in the prompt

explanation: Models produce likely wording, not checked facts. That is why you check against sources.

questionText: The draft says "budget EUR 18 million"; the decision minutes say "EUR 1.8 million for the pilot". Which status?

answerOptions.text: supported
missing: delete it
irrelevant, the order of magnitude is roughly right
contradicted: correct it

explanation: The source says something else: a factor of ten and the wrong scope. You correct to the supported wording.

questionText: What is a primary source for a revenue figure?

answerOptions.text: The report or system that records the figure
A second language model
A blog post quoting the figure
A colleague's memory

explanation: The primary source is the document that records the fact. There you check definition, period, unit and date.

questionText: Which factors set the review depth of an AI output?

answerOptions.text: Length of the text and time of day
Impact of an error, reversibility and audience
Model name and price
How confident the text sounds

explanation: The more consequential, irreversible and public, the more thoroughly you check.

questionText: An AI draft is to promise a customer a refund. What is the fitting control?

answerOptions.text: Proofread quickly and send
Have a second model check the text
Check facts against sources and have the responsible person approve the commitment
Nothing, the commitment is politely worded

explanation: Money, external, hard to reverse: the highest review level with sign-off. A second model replaces neither source nor authority.

questionText: What is shadow AI?

answerOptions.text: An AI model that runs at night
Any AI use in dark mode
A prohibited AI practice under the EU AI Act
AI use for work outside approved tools and controls

explanation: It includes private chat accounts, browser extensions, new features in bought software and personal API keys.

questionText: What does Article 4 of the EU AI Act require in the version in force?

answerOptions.text: Providers and deployers take measures that support the AI literacy of their staff, matched to context and prior knowledge.
Every person needs an AI certificate.
A mandatory course with a fixed number of hours.
Only makers of AI models are affected.

explanation: Article 4 has applied since 2 February 2025 and prescribes neither a format nor a certificate.

questionText: An employee accidentally entered salary data into an unapproved AI service. What is the right first step?

answerOptions.text: Delete the history and say nothing
Report internally at once and secure time, tool, data and output
Wait and see whether anything happens
Overwrite the data in the tool

explanation: The controller assesses whether the supervisory authority must be notified (GDPR Art. 33). For that they need the secured facts.

questionText: Your office software gets a new AI feature through an update. From when may you use it with confidential data?

answerOptions.text: Immediately, the software has already been bought
As soon as it is enabled by default
When the feature is approved for the purpose and data class
After a week without problems

explanation: Approvals cover features and configurations, not product names.

questionText: When is an AI use policy ready for approval?

answerOptions.text: As soon as the text is written
When it is at least ten pages long
When an AI tool has checked it
When every placeholder is replaced and the responsible functions have agreed

explanation: An open placeholder such as the reporting channel makes the policy useless when it counts. Depending on the organization, data protection, information security and the works council agree.
